confirmed_issues.quote_a: If the club changed KES 5,000 to dollars and back, would it get KES 5,000 back? Estimate before we test it in Lesson 8.
confirmed_issues.problem: Lesson 7 says this KES 5,000 round trip will be tested in Lesson 8, but Lesson 8 never tests or calculates it. Lesson 8 only reuses Mr Brooks's USD 100 round trip.
confirmed_issues.correct_value: Remove the reference to Lesson 8, or add the KES 5,000 round-trip calculation to Lesson 8.

confirmed_issues.quote_a: Mr Brooks paid the margin once at each change. Where did his USD 1.16 go?
confirmed_issues.problem: The lesson defines the margin as the whole KES 1.50 per USD gap between the buying and selling rates. A round trip (buy at 128.00, sell back at 129.50) loses that gap only once in total: 1 - 128/129.50 ≈ 1.16%, which gives USD 98.84. If the full margin were paid at each of the two changes, the loss would be about double. So the statement contradicts the lesson's own USD 98.84 result.
confirmed_issues.correct_value: Over the round trip Mr Brooks loses the KES 1.50-per-USD spread once in total: 100 × (1 − 128/129.50) ≈ USD 1.16.
confirmed_issues.reference: Round-trip loss = spread once: 100 × (1 − 128/129.50) ≈ USD 1.16; the buy/sell spread is the dealer's margin.
